tasks.task: Ask what was found outside subscriptions and why one discovered item ranks where it does.

steps.description: Find the discovered item by its topic terms.
steps.observed: search_items returned the discovered item when queried by its topic terms

steps.description: List items found outside followed subscriptions with origin and original URL.
steps.observed: get_discoveries listed the item with origin 'discovered' and its original URL

steps.description: Read the item with its model analysis provenance, references and latest score.
steps.observed: get_item returned the item with latest_score present (true) and 1 recorded source references (analysis status analysed)

steps.description: Explain why the item ranks as it does, with components and exclusions.
steps.observed: explain_ranking returned 1 recorded scoring run(s) with criteria versions and exclusion reasons (1 exclusions)

tasks.shipped: The connecting MCP client performs the explanation conversationally: search_items and get_discoveries surface the discovery with origin provenance, get_item reads analysis provenance and source references, explain_ranking returns the recorded scoring runs, criteria version and exclusions. A browser would re-render the same recorded rows in a second transport.

tasks.task: Run one new budgeted discovery query and see what it found.

steps.description: Preview the bounded query with its budget reservation.
steps.observed: preview returned run_one_budgeted_query with a single-use confirm token

steps.description: Confirm; the run re-checks budgets and pace against the recorded provider.
steps.observed: confirm dispatched status complete over 1 page(s) and ingested 1 result(s) from the recorded provider (2 provider request(s) in total)

steps.description: See the new discovered items with origin and original URLs.
steps.cliVerb: discovery-runs + search QUERY (run ledger and canonical items; origin provenance is MCP-only)
steps.observed: the discovery ledger grew from 2 to 3 recorded result(s); get_discoveries lists the new items

tasks.shipped: trigger_discovery preview/confirm performs the budgeted dispatch through the shared application service (the same preview/confirm and budget ledger the CLI verbs discovery-trigger-preview/discovery-trigger-confirm use), and get_discoveries reports the new findings with origin provenance.

tasks.task: Read the active interests and change what the user values.

steps.observed: get_interests returned the seeded active interest (latest version, persistent)

steps.description: Preview the new immutable interest version.
steps.observed: preview recorded effect append_version toward version 2 with a confirmation token

steps.description: Confirm; scores are re-derived, frozen editions unchanged.
steps.observed: the confirmed update appended the new immutable version visible to get_interests

steps.description: Replay a consumed confirmation token and expect rejection.
steps.observed: the replayed token was rejected; confirmation stays single-use and bound to the previewed payload over every transport

tasks.shipped: get_interests reads profiles; update_interest preview/confirm appends the next immutable version through the shared application service (the same previewUpdateInterest/confirmUpdateInterest the CLI interest-preview/interest-confirm verbs call). A web form would add an input field, not a capability.

tasks.task: Give explicit useful feedback on a discovery result so scoring and query order refine.

steps.description: Preview recording explicit feedback for the item.
steps.observed: preview returned the item title (Humanoid firmware advisory affects bench tests) with a confirmation token
get_feedback lists the recorded latest judgment for the item with source mcp
the shipped feedback write recorded 1 discovery-result refinement row(s) for the item, so future query order refines with provenance (the CLI discovery-item-feedback verb writes the same ledger)

tasks.shipped: submit_feedback preview/confirm records the explicit judgment through the shared feedback service, visible over get_feedback, and the same write propagates the item/query/discovery refinement to the discovery-result ledger (the CLI feedback-preview/feedback-confirm and discovery-item-feedback verbs call the identical application service).

tasks.task: Review one story development end to end: coverage, recorded change evidence and the frozen edition it was published in.

steps.description: Find both items covering the development.
Read the development group with its members and citations.
steps.observed: get_story_group returned the development with its recorded memberships and citations

steps.description: Read recorded change evidence for the development.
steps.observed: get_development_changes returned 2 recorded events (new coverage and content changes) inside the 3-day window

steps.description: Read the immutable edition the development was published in.
steps.observed: frozen view returned the edition frozen near 2026-11-10T07:00:00.000Z with the development's item reference, and the list view returned 1 edition(s)

steps.description: Give not-useful edition feedback and re-read the frozen edition.
steps.observed: the not-useful edition feedback was recorded with its edition context while the frozen edition bytes stayed identical

tasks.shipped: The development and history review is covered by the read tools (get_story_group, get_development_changes, get_digest frozen/list) plus the confirmed feedback mutation through the same application service the CLI feedback verbs call; the connecting MCP client narrates the review.

newTrustBoundariesAdoptionWouldCreate: an authenticated, browser-session HTTP surface rendered from untrusted stored content (a new origin/CSRF and HTML-sanitisation boundary the MCP transport does not need)
browser session state re-implementing the preview/confirm mutation contract that already exists transport-free
a second rendering of recorded data whose only unique input is already fully exposed to the conversational client

adoption.threshold: Adopt a minimal discovery-focused web interface only when the replayed corpus contains at least one concrete task step that no shipped MCP tool and no shipped CLI verb can perform, and a private, authenticated browser session would demonstrably and materially improve exactly that step within the modular-monolith constraints (reusing the shared application services, keeping the preview/confirm mutation contract, origin/CSRF protections and untrusted-content citation discipline), rather than duplicating conversational reasoning or read rendering the connecting MCP client already performs. Otherwise record a justified non-adoption.
